definitions.explanation: Soft or pureed food given to infants as they transition from breast milk or formula to solid food, typically starting around 5-6 months of age.

examples.japanese: {離乳食|りにゅうしょく}を{始|はじ}めた。
{離乳食|りにゅうしょく}は{手作|てづく}りしている。
examples.english: I make the baby food by hand.

examples.japanese: {生後|せいご}5か{月|げつ}ごろから{離乳食|りにゅうしょく}を{少|すこ}しずつ{与|あた}えていく。
examples.english: From around five months after birth, you gradually introduce weaning food.

notes:
{離乳食|りにゅうしょく} literally means "weaning food" — {離乳|りにゅう} (weaning) + {食|しょく} (food). In Japan, {離乳食|りにゅうしょく} typically progresses through stages from smooth purees to chunkier textures.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {離乳食|りにゅうしょく}を{始|はじ}める (to start weaning food)
- {離乳食|りにゅうしょく}を{作|つく}る (to make baby food)
- {離乳食|りにゅうしょく}レシピ (baby food recipes)
- {離乳食|りにゅうしょく}の{進|すす}め{方|かた} (how to introduce weaning food)

USAGE:
This is an essential parenting vocabulary word in Japan. Japanese bookstores have entire sections dedicated to {離乳食|りにゅうしょく} cookbooks and guides. The word appears constantly in parenting magazines, pediatric clinic pamphlets, and online parenting forums.
